passage:
Coach's notebook, college cricket, 18 November
Talked with Hemant after nets today. Last month Nikhil told the selectors Hemant had skipped training, which wasn't true, and Hemant lost his place. Hemant has barely spoken to him since.
Today Hemant said something new. He had overheard Nikhil on the phone with his father, being shouted at about the sports scholarship. 'He was scared, Coach. He'd lose the fees if he got dropped.'
Then he added quickly, 'It's still not okay, what he did.'
I agreed with both parts. Understanding why doesn't make it right.
He seemed looser in the shoulders than he has in weeks, and bowled well.
Next step: I'll raise the false report with the selectors myself, and ask Hemant if he wants me there when he talks to Nikhil.
- Raghav

qa.q: What false thing did Nikhil tell the selectors?
qa.a: Nikhil told them Hemant had skipped training.

qa.q: What does Hemant's quick 'It's still not okay' show?
qa.a: It shows he understands Nikhil's fear without excusing the lie, holding both at once.

qa.q: What does Raghav plan next, and why is it fair?
qa.a: Raghav will raise the false report with the selectors and offer to be there if Hemant talks to Nikhil, so understanding doesn't mean the wrong goes unaddressed.

qa.q: What might Nikhil have been experiencing when his father shouted about the scholarship?
qa.a: Nikhil was likely frightened of losing his fees and under heavy pressure, which may have pushed him into the lie.

grounding: It shows a young man beginning to understand a teammate's fear and pressure without excusing the lie, and his bitterness loosening.

subtype: Stage 4: Seeing the other as human [Actor]
passage:
Sunday night
Gurleen's cousin told me today why she didn't turn up for my college interview in May, after promising to drive me. I waited at the gate for forty minutes and missed my slot. I've hated her since.
Turns out that morning her dad was taken to hospital, and she was so ashamed of the scene at home she couldn't tell anyone. Not even me.
I sat on the steps for a long time after hearing that.
I'm still angry. She could have sent one text. That's true and I'm not pretending it isn't.
But I can see her now: panicking, embarrassed, nineteen, with no good choices. She's not the villain I built up in my head. She's a person who messed up on the worst day of her life.
It's weird. The bitterness feels looser. Not gone.
- Kishore

qa.q: How long did Kishore wait at the gate?
qa.a: Kishore waited at the gate for forty minutes.

qa.q: How does Kishore feel after hearing what happened to Gurleen?
qa.a: Still angry that one text was never sent, but the bitterness has loosened as Kishore understands her panic and shame.

qa.q: Why doesn't understanding mean Kishore has to excuse Gurleen?
qa.a: Kishore can see why she failed to turn up while still holding that she could have sent a text; understanding eases bitterness without approving the act.

qa.q: What might Gurleen have been going through that morning?
qa.a: She was likely panicking about her dad and ashamed of the scene at home, feeling unable to tell anyone.

grounding: It shows someone coming to understand a friend's panic and shame on a hard day without excusing the broken promise, and feeling bitterness loosen.
